html:
An ancient port and bead-making town on the Coromandel coast, about 4 kilometres from Pondicherry in south India. It was busy from about the 2nd century BCE to the 2nd century CE.

Mortimer Wheeler dug there in 1945 and found Roman pottery, including fine red Arretine ware and wine amphorae from the Mediterranean. This was hard proof of the trade with the Roman Empire that Greek and Roman writers describe. Scholars link it with Poduke, a market named in the Periplus of the Erythraean Sea.

The town also made glass and stone beads, which were traded across the Bay of Bengal into Southeast Asia. It belonged to the world of the Tamil kingdoms, whose ports, like Muziris on the west coast, drew ships that sailed with the monsoon winds after Roman ships reached India.
